  • Troubleshooting
    • Commits not collected, but Issues and Pull Requests are collected
    • Monitor dashboard renders slowly on a large fleet
    • Search keystrokes freeze the dashboard at 100K repos
    • /api/queue endpoint slow or returns huge JSON
    • Token invalidation (401 vs 403)
      • HTTP 401 Bad Credentials
      • HTTP 403 Forbidden / Rate Limited
      • rate limit exhausted repeats for one key while other keys have budget
      • Observation lines added in 0.29.70
    • FK constraint violations
    • “No API keys configured” / Startup failure
    • “Commit resolution FAILED”
    • “No data collected”
    • unsupported Unicode escape sequence (SQLSTATE 22P05)
    • “Pull requests / contributors / events: not found” or “forbidden”
    • Gap-filled historical issues/PRs have no comments
    • Gap-fill failure on large repos persists across multiple cycles
    • Metadata shows issues/PRs but gathered count stays at 0
    • Repeated “unexpected status 301” retries on moved/renamed repos
    • HTTP 410 Gone on individual issues / PRs
    • GitLab repo_info.commit_count is 0 but facade found commits
    • Release collection “not found” errors
    • Git clone exit status 128
    • Garbage timestamps (year 0001 BC)
    • Schema version mismatch: web, api and the scancode worker refuse to start
    • Null byte errors in text fields
    • Scancode produces no results / scanned-repo count barely advances (corrupt libmagic)
    • PostgreSQL restarts nightly — aveloxis.log floods with “database system is shutting down”
    • process stalled — the whole collector stops for seconds at a time
    • Brief “database unavailable” blips that aren’t real outages (connect/SASL-auth timeouts)

API reference

Every operation of the Aveloxis REST API, grouped by area. This page is rendered from openapi.yaml when the documentation is built; the conventions explain the shared rules (access, errors, rate limits, caching) that each entry assumes. Each entry names its operation (operationId), states who may call it, and ends with the handler that serves it in internal/api.

Service

Liveness and the anonymous fleet figures.

GET /api/v1/health
Operation:

health

Access:

public: no token is needed.

Returns the server’s status and version.

The liveness probe. It reads nothing from the database.

Handler: handleHealth.

Response JSON Object:

  • status (string, required)

  • version (string, required) – The running binary’s version.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The process is serving.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

GET /api/v1/public/stats
Operation:

publicFleetStats

Access:

public: no token is needed.

Returns the fleet’s repository, commit, issue, pull-request and contributor totals.

The landing page’s anonymous figures. Served from a 60-second cache that keeps the last good values when a reload fails.

Handler: handlePublicStats.

Response JSON Object:

  • repos (integer:int64, required) – Every repository in the catalog, archived ones included.

  • commits (integer:int64, required) – Sum of the collection queue’s cached gathered commit totals.

  • issues (integer:int64, required)

  • prs (integer:int64, required)

  • contributors (integer:int64, required) – The contributor catalog’s row count.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The totals.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – stats unavailable (text) when the first load since the process started failed and no earlier values exist; or a presented token could not be checked (JSON, session lookup failed; try again); or the request ran past http_timeout_seconds (text, request exceeded http_timeout_seconds).

GET /api/v1/mailing-list/stats
Operation:

mailingListStats

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the mailing-list collection coverage rollup.

The same figures as aveloxis mailing-list-stats. The keys are PascalCase.

Cost: counts over the mailing-list tables on every call (not cached).

Handler: handleMailingListStats.

Response JSON Object:

  • Lists (integer, required) – Registered lists.

  • ScanComplete (integer, required) – Lists that finished their current scan.

  • EmailMessages (integer:int64, required)

  • Mirrors (integer:int64, required)

  • SignaledCaptured (integer:int64, required) – Messages that named a repository.

  • SignaledResolved (integer:int64, required) – Of those, the ones resolved to a collected repository.

  • SenderTotal (integer:int64, required)

  • SenderResolved (integer:int64, required)

  • ByClass (object, required) – Message count per msg_class; null when no message is classified. Or null.

  • ByClass.{msg_class} (integer:int64) – One entry per {msg_class}.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The rollup.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Repositories

One collected repository’s statistics, series, licenses, SBOMs, scan results and traffic.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/stats
Operation:

repositoryStats

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns a repository’s gathered and forge-reported counts, vulnerability counts and status.

Gathered counts are the collection queue’s cached totals; metadata counts come from the latest forge snapshot. An id with no repository answers zeros to an unscoped caller (a scoped caller gets the 403).

Handler: handleRepoStats.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Response JSON Object:

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • gathered_prs (integer, required) – Pull requests collected, from the collection queue’s cached totals as of the last completed collection.

  • gathered_issues (integer, required)

  • gathered_commits (integer, required)

  • metadata_prs (integer, required) – The forge’s reported total from the latest metadata snapshot.

  • metadata_issues (integer, required)

  • metadata_commits (integer, required)

  • vulnerabilities (integer, required) – Current findings (unresolved, not the repository’s own package, version known).

  • critical_vulns (integer, required) – Current findings with severity CRITICAL or a CVSS score of at least 9.0.

  • vulnerabilities_version_unknown (integer, required) – Findings matched against an unpinned version.

  • archived (boolean) – Single-repository answer only. The forge reports the repository as archived (read-only). The batch answer (/repos/stats) does not read it and always says false.

  • last_activity_at (string:date-time) – Single-repository answer only. The latest observed activity; absent when unknown (and always absent in the batch answer).

  • forked_from (string) – Single-repository answer only (always absent in the batch answer). The upstream owner/name of a fork; (unknown upstream) when the forge reports a fork but not its upstream; absent otherwise.

  • last_collected (string:date-time)

  • gone_at (string:date-time) – When the forge stopped serving the repository; absent while it is served.

  • unavailable_reason (string) – The forge’s own message for a blocked or disabled repository.

  • unavailable_url (string) – The https link that message gives.

  • metadata_as_of (string:date-time) – The date of the metadata snapshot behind the metadata_* counts.

  • forge_id_changes[] (object) – A recorded forge-ID change (db.ForgeIDChange).

  • forge_id_changes[].repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • forge_id_changes[].old_forge_id (string, required)

  • forge_id_changes[].new_forge_id (string, required)

  • forge_id_changes[].first_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • forge_id_changes[].last_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • forge_id_changes[].forge_created_at (string:date-time) – When the forge created the new repository; absent when the scan did not list it.

  • forge_id_changes[].adopted_at (string:date-time) – Adopted changes only.

  • forge_id_changes[].adopted_by (string)

  • forge_id_changes[].note (string)

  • forge_id_changes[].repo_git (string) – The repository’s stored URL.

  • forge_id_changes[].superseded (boolean) – A pending change whose old ID is no longer the stored one; it cannot be adopted. Absent when false.

  • has_metadata_snapshot (boolean) – Present (true) when a metadata snapshot exists, even one without a date.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The repository’s statistics.

  • 400 Bad Request – The request is malformed (an id that is not an integer, a value outside its enum, a missing parameter). Shared response BadRequest.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/stats
Operation:

repositoryStatsBatch

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the statistics of several repositories, keyed by id.

ids is a comma-separated list of repository ids; an entry that is not a positive integer is a 400 (since 0.29.99; it was skipped before). At most 500 ids per request. A caller that is not an administrator’s session (an API token, or any other signed-in session) gets only the ids in its groups; the others are left out, and an answer with none of them is {}. An id no repository has is left out too (since 0.29.99; it was a row of zeros). Repositories no longer in the collection queue fall back to live counts.

Handler: handleRepoStatsBatch.

Query Parameters:

  • ids (string, required) – Comma-separated repository ids, at most 500.

Response JSON Object:

  • {repo_id} (object) – One entry per {repo_id}.

  • {repo_id}.repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • {repo_id}.gathered_prs (integer, required) – Pull requests collected, from the collection queue’s cached totals as of the last completed collection.

  • {repo_id}.gathered_issues (integer, required)

  • {repo_id}.gathered_commits (integer, required)

  • {repo_id}.metadata_prs (integer, required) – The forge’s reported total from the latest metadata snapshot.

  • {repo_id}.metadata_issues (integer, required)

  • {repo_id}.metadata_commits (integer, required)

  • {repo_id}.vulnerabilities (integer, required) – Current findings (unresolved, not the repository’s own package, version known).

  • {repo_id}.critical_vulns (integer, required) – Current findings with severity CRITICAL or a CVSS score of at least 9.0.

  • {repo_id}.vulnerabilities_version_unknown (integer, required) – Findings matched against an unpinned version.

  • {repo_id}.archived (boolean) – Single-repository answer only. The forge reports the repository as archived (read-only). The batch answer (/repos/stats) does not read it and always says false.

  • {repo_id}.last_activity_at (string:date-time) – Single-repository answer only. The latest observed activity; absent when unknown (and always absent in the batch answer).

  • {repo_id}.forked_from (string) – Single-repository answer only (always absent in the batch answer). The upstream owner/name of a fork; (unknown upstream) when the forge reports a fork but not its upstream; absent otherwise.

  • {repo_id}.last_collected (string:date-time)

  • {repo_id}.gone_at (string:date-time) – When the forge stopped serving the repository; absent while it is served.

  • {repo_id}.unavailable_reason (string) – The forge’s own message for a blocked or disabled repository.

  • {repo_id}.unavailable_url (string) – The https link that message gives.

  • {repo_id}.metadata_as_of (string:date-time) – The date of the metadata snapshot behind the metadata_* counts.

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[] (object) – A recorded forge-ID change (db.ForgeIDChange).

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].old_forge_id (string, required)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].new_forge_id (string, required)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].first_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].last_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].forge_created_at (string:date-time) – When the forge created the new repository; absent when the scan did not list it.

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].adopted_at (string:date-time) – Adopted changes only.

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].adopted_by (string)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].note (string)

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].repo_git (string) – The repository’s stored URL.

  • {repo_id}.forge_id_changes[].superseded (boolean) – A pending change whose old ID is no longer the stored one; it cannot be adopted. Absent when false.

  • {repo_id}.has_metadata_snapshot (boolean) – Present (true) when a metadata snapshot exists, even one without a date.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – Statistics per repository id (object keys are the ids as strings).

  • 400 Bad Request – ids missing, an entry that is not a positive integer, or more than 500 ids.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/sbom
Operation:

repositorySBOM

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns a software bill of materials for a repository as a JSON download.

Generated from the stored dependency data: CycloneDX 1.7 (default) or SPDX 2.3. Repositories with lockfile data carry the real dependency graph. The Content-Disposition filename is sbom-repo-<id>[-runtime][-with-vulns].cdx.json or .spdx.json.

Cost: generated per request when not in the response cache.

Handler: handleSBOMDownload.

Request Headers:

  • If-None-Match (string) – An ETag from an earlier answer. When it names the current one the answer is 304 with no body.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • format (string:enum)

  • scope (string:enum) – runtime keeps only runtime-scope components (unclassified count as runtime).

  • vulns (string) – 1 annotates the document with the repository’s current findings (CycloneDX vulnerabilities; SPDX package externalRefs of category SECURITY). Any other value is ignored.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The SBOM document.

  • 304 Not Modified – The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. Shared response NotModified.

  • 400 Bad Request – An id that is not a positive integer, or format / scope outside their values.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – repo not found (an unscoped caller asked for an id with no repository).

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • Content-Disposition (string) – attachment; filename="…".

  • ETag (string) – The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

  • Cache-Control (string:enum) – no-cache for an answer any caller may be given (revalidate each time); private, no-store for an answer about this caller, which nothing may store.

  • X-Cache (string) – hit when the answer came from the server’s response cache; absent otherwise.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/timeseries
Operation:

repositoryTimeSeries

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns a repository’s weekly commits, pull requests opened and merged, and issues opened.

The window starts two years before today’s UTC midnight by default. An omitted until ends it at the latest plausible commit time, UTC midnight two days ahead; a given until is inclusive (the window ends at the next midnight) and is never later than that bound. The start is never earlier than 1970-01-02. The bounds apply to all four series, not only commits. Weeks start on Monday (UTC).

Handler: handleTimeSeries.

Request Headers:

  • If-None-Match (string) – An ETag from an earlier answer. When it names the current one the answer is 304 with no body.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • since (string:date) – First UTC day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). A value that does not parse is a 400 (since 0.29.99; it fell back to the default before).

  • until (string:date) – Last UTC day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive: the whole day counts). A value that does not parse is a 400 (since 0.29.99). A window whose since is not before until is a 400.

Response JSON Object:

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • repo_name (string, required)

  • repo_owner (string, required)

  • commits[] (object) – One week of the repository time series. Its number is count, the one native series that predates the value convention (see the conventions page, “One field name for a metric’s number”); /compare and the Augur-compatible metrics carry value.

  • commits[].week_start (string:date-time, required) – The Monday that starts the week (UTC).

  • commits[].count (integer, required)

  • prs_opened[] (object) – One week of the repository time series. Its number is count, the one native series that predates the value convention (see the conventions page, “One field name for a metric’s number”); /compare and the Augur-compatible metrics carry value.

  • prs_opened[].week_start (string:date-time, required) – The Monday that starts the week (UTC).

  • prs_opened[].count (integer, required)

  • prs_merged[] (object) – One week of the repository time series. Its number is count, the one native series that predates the value convention (see the conventions page, “One field name for a metric’s number”); /compare and the Augur-compatible metrics carry value.

  • prs_merged[].week_start (string:date-time, required) – The Monday that starts the week (UTC).

  • prs_merged[].count (integer, required)

  • issues[] (object) – One week of the repository time series. Its number is count, the one native series that predates the value convention (see the conventions page, “One field name for a metric’s number”); /compare and the Augur-compatible metrics carry value.

  • issues[].week_start (string:date-time, required) – The Monday that starts the week (UTC).

  • issues[].count (integer, required)

  • 200 OK – The four weekly series.

  • 304 Not Modified – The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. Shared response NotModified.

  • 400 Bad Request – An id that is not a positive integer, a date that does not parse, or since not before until.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure; also an unscoped caller’s id with no repository.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • ETag (string) – The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/traffic
Operation:

repositoryTraffic

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns a repository’s stored traffic history.

Everything stored from the forge’s traffic and statistics APIs, in one answer without paging: every daily row of clones and views, every 14-day window and complete week, and the latest top paths and referrers. A day with a row was read, even when its counts are 0. A GitLab repository answers its daily clones with uniques null, empty lists for the rest and a null snapshot_date. So does a repository whose key the forge refuses, and an id with no repository, to an unscoped caller (a scoped caller gets the 403). Grows by about 730 daily rows a year; the read is indexed by repository.

Handler: handleRepoTraffic.

Request Headers:

  • If-None-Match (string) – An ETag from an earlier answer. When it names the current one the answer is 304 with no body.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Response JSON Object:

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • clones[] (object) – One stored UTC day of clones or views (db.TrafficDay).

  • clones[].date (string:date, required)

  • clones[].count (integer, null, required) – Clones or views that day.

  • clones[].uniques (integer, null, required) – Distinct cloners or visitors that day; null when the forge does not count them (GitLab clones).

  • views[] (object) – One stored UTC day of clones or views (db.TrafficDay).

  • views[].date (string:date, required)

  • views[].count (integer, null, required, required) – Clones or views that day.

  • views[].uniques (integer, null, required, required) – Distinct cloners or visitors that day; null when the forge does not count them (GitLab clones).

  • windows[] (object) – One 14-day window GitHub reported, from its first to its last daily bucket (db.TrafficWindow).

  • windows[].kind (string:enum, required)

  • windows[].start (string:date, required)

  • windows[].end (string:date, required) – The window’s last day, included.

  • windows[].uniques (integer, null, required) – Distinct visitors or cloners over the window, as GitHub computes them; not the sum of the daily uniques.

  • weeks[] (object) – One complete Monday-to-Sunday week inside a read’s window (db.TrafficWeek).

  • weeks[].kind (string:enum, required)

  • weeks[].week_start (string:date, required) – The week’s Monday.

  • weeks[].uniques (integer, null, required) – Distinct visitors or cloners over the week.

  • snapshot_date (['string', 'null']:date, required) – The latest UTC collection date that stored a path or a referrer; paths and referrers are that date’s snapshot. null when none was ever stored.

  • paths[] (object) – One of the top paths GitHub reported for its 14-day period (db.TrafficPath).

  • paths[].path (string, required)

  • paths[].title (string, required)

  • paths[].count (integer, null, required) – Views of the path over GitHub’s 14-day period.

  • paths[].uniques (integer, null, required) – Distinct visitors of the path over that period.

  • referrers[] (object) – One of the top referring sites GitHub reported for its 14-day period (db.TrafficReferrer).

  • referrers[].referrer (string, required)

  • referrers[].count (integer, null, required) – Views the site sent over GitHub’s 14-day period.

  • referrers[].uniques (integer, null, required) – Distinct visitors the site sent over that period.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Stars are the caller’s own; no repository scope applies.

PUT /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/star
Operation:

starRepository

Access:

a signed-in session or an API token.

Stars a repository for the caller.

A signed-in session starring a repository outside its groups adds it to its “Starred” group (added_to_group), counted against shared_with_me_adds_per_hour (429), the repository allocation (403) and the daily additions (429, quota repo_links_per_day). An API token is refused for such a repository with the instructions to add it. Starring again is idempotent.

Handler: handleStarRepo.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Response JSON Object:

  • ok (boolean, required)

  • starred (boolean, required) – true after a star, false after an unstar.

  • added_to_group (string) – Present when this star added the repository to the caller’s “Starred” group.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – Starred.

  • 400 Bad Request – The request is malformed (an id that is not an integer, a value outside its enum, a missing parameter). Shared response BadRequest.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Vulnerabilities

Vulnerability findings and the OpenSSF Scorecard.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/vulnerabilities
Operation:

repositoryVulnerabilities

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns a repository’s vulnerability findings, current and resolved, with their counts.

Every finding the OSV scans recorded for the repository’s dependencies. A finding with resolved_at is history. counts classifies each finding once: resolved; self (an advisory about the repository’s own package); unknown_version (an unpinned range, except GitHub Actions refs); otherwise current, split into direct/transitive and runtime/dev, with critical (severity CRITICAL or CVSS 9.0 and up) counted within current and unknown_version_critical within unknown_version.

Current transitive findings carry introduced_by when the repository’s lockfiles give the dependency edges. When the edge or certainty lookups fail, the findings are still served, without that part, and the answer is not cached.

Handler: handleRepoVulnerabilities.

Request Headers:

  • If-None-Match (string) – An ETag from an earlier answer. When it names the current one the answer is 304 with no body.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Response JSON Object:

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • vulnerabilities[] (object) – One vulnerability finding (vulnJSON).

  • vulnerabilities[].vuln_id (string, required) – The OSV id (GHSA, PYSEC, GO, …).

  • vulnerabilities[].cve_id (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].package_name (string, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].package_purl (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].ecosystem (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].severity (string, required) – The advisory’s severity word as stored (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM/MODERATE, LOW), or empty.

  • vulnerabilities[].cvss_score (number, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].cvss_vector (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].summary (string, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].details (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].scanned_version (string) – The version the scan matched, read from package_purl’s @version; absent when the purl carries none.

  • vulnerabilities[].fixed_version (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].introduced_version (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].source (string, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].aliases[] (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].advisory_url (string:uri, required) – The OSV page.

  • vulnerabilities[].cve_url (string:uri) – The OpenCVE page, when there is a CVE id.

  • vulnerabilities[].first_detected_at (string:date-time, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].last_seen_at (string:date-time, required)

  • vulnerabilities[].resolved_at (string:date-time) – When the finding stopped being seen. Absent while the repository is still affected.

  • vulnerabilities[].declared_requirement (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].version_resolution (string) – How the scanned version was obtained (for example unpinned when the manifest named a range and no lockfile pinned it).

  • vulnerabilities[].dependency_kind (string) – direct, transitive, or self (an advisory about the repository’s own package).

  • vulnerabilities[].introduced_by[] (object) – How a direct dependency pulls a vulnerable package in (vulnChainJSON).

  • vulnerabilities[].introduced_by[].root (string, required) – The direct dependency.

  • vulnerabilities[].introduced_by[].chain[] (string)

  • vulnerabilities[].introduced_by_total_roots (integer) – How many direct dependencies pull the package in (all of them, not only the ones in introduced_by).

  • vulnerabilities[].dependency_scope (string) – The dependency’s scope (runtime, dev, test, build, optional, peer); empty counts as runtime.

  • scanned_at (['string', 'null']:date-time, required) – The last vulnerability scan; null when never scanned (an empty list then means “not scanned”, not “no findings”).

  • lockfile_certainty (object, required) – How much of the repository’s dependency set a lockfile pins (db.LockfileCertainty).

  • lockfile_certainty.overall (string:enum, required)

  • lockfile_certainty.ecosystems[] (object)

  • lockfile_certainty.ecosystems[].ecosystem (string, required)

  • lockfile_certainty.ecosystems[].lockfile_kind (string, required) – The lockfile format (go.mod for Go, which pins by construction).

  • lockfile_certainty.ecosystems[].locked_packages (integer, required)

  • counts (object, required)

  • counts.current (integer, required)

  • counts.resolved (integer, required)

  • counts.critical (integer, required)

  • counts.direct (integer, required)

  • counts.transitive (integer, required)

  • counts.dev (integer, required)

  • counts.runtime (integer, required)

  • counts.self (integer, required)

  • counts.unknown_version (integer, required)

  • counts.unknown_version_critical (integer, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The findings.

  • 304 Not Modified – The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. Shared response NotModified.

  • 400 Bad Request – The request is malformed (an id that is not an integer, a value outside its enum, a missing parameter). Shared response BadRequest.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • ETag (string) – The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

  • Cache-Control (string:enum) – no-cache for an answer any caller may be given (revalidate each time); private, no-store for an answer about this caller, which nothing may store.

  • X-Cache (string) – hit when the answer came from the server’s response cache; absent otherwise.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

scanned is false (and checks []) when no Scorecard run is stored. mode is remote for the complete check set, local for the subset Scorecard computes from a clone alone, and empty for a scan that predates the distinction. overall is absent for scans stored before the aggregate was kept.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

Its value is the group’s name. Who contributes to a repository, and where else they are active.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/contributions/identities
Operation:

repositoryContributorIdentities

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns every distinct person who contributed to a repository in the window.

A contribution is a commit authored, an issue opened or closed, an issue or pull-request event, a pull request opened, a review submitted, or any comment. Commits whose author was never resolved to a contributor are not counted. The window defaults to the last two years; ordered by login then full name.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/contributors/elsewhere
Operation:

repositoryContributorsElsewhere

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the other repositories where a repository’s top contributors are active.

For the top contributors (same ranking as repositoryTopContributors), up to ten other repositories each from the contributors’ GitHub daily history. For an API token, collected repositories outside its owner’s groups are left out; repositories not collected here stay. Answers are cached for 60 seconds.

Handler: handleContributorsElsewhere.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • since (string:date) – First day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD); defaults to 180 days ago. A value that does not parse is a 400 (since 0.29.99).

  • limit (integer) – Contributors to return; values that are not positive integers mean the default, larger values are capped at 25.

  • bots (string) – hide leaves out automation accounts, as in repositoryTopContributors.

Response JSON Object:

  • since (string:date, required)

  • limit (integer, required)

  • contributors[] (object)

  • contributors[].cntrb_id (string:uuid, required)

  • contributors[].login (string, required)

  • contributors[].backfilled_at (['string', 'null']:date-time, required) – null while the history backfill has not reached this contributor: an empty elsewhere then means “pending”, not “nowhere else”. Automation accounts stay null by design.

  • contributors[].elsewhere[] (object)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].repo_full_name (string, required)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].repo_id (integer:int64) – Present only when the repository is collected on this instance.

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].active_days (integer, required)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].commits (integer, required)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].issues (integer, required)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].prs (integer, required)

  • contributors[].elsewhere[].reviews (integer, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The contributors and their other repositories.

  • 400 Bad Request – The request is malformed (an id that is not an integer, a value outside its enum, a missing parameter). Shared response BadRequest.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

Operation:

contributorActivity

Access:

a signed-in session or an API token.

Returns one contributor’s monthly activity per repository and daily contribution totals.

Requires an identity but no repository scope: the history spans repositories this instance does not collect. For an API token, collected repositories outside its owner’s groups are left out. Answers are cached for 60 seconds.

Handler: handleContributorActivity.

Parameters:

Query Parameters:

  • bucket (string) – Only month is accepted (reserved for other granularities).

  • backfilled_at (['string', 'null']:date-time, required) – Same meaning as in ElsewhereContributor.

  • months (integer, required) – The window in months, after the cap.

  • repos[] (object)

  • repos[].repo_full_name (string, required)

  • repos[].repo_id (integer:int64) – Present only when the repository is collected on this instance.

  • repos[].months[] (object)

  • repos[].months[].month (string, required) – YYYY-MM.

  • repos[].months[].active_days (integer, required)

  • repos[].months[].commits (integer, required)

  • repos[].months[].issues (integer, required)

  • repos[].months[].prs (integer, required)

Status Codes:

  • 400 Bad Request – cntrbID is not a UUID, or bucket is not month.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

Comparison

The metric catalog and the comparison of up to seven repositories or organizations.

GET /api/v1/metrics
Operation:

metricCatalog

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the comparison metric catalog.

The definitions behind GET /api/v1/compare and GET /api/v1/compare/snapshot, with what each improves on the CHAOSS metric it follows. Constant for a release; sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600.

Handler: handleMetricsCatalog.

Response JSON Object:

  • branding (string, required)

  • metrics[] (object) – One metric of the comparison catalog (MetricDef).

  • metrics[].id (string, required) – The value to pass as metric.

  • metrics[].name (string, required)

  • metrics[].definition (string, required)

  • metrics[].unit (string, required)

  • metrics[].kind (string:enum, required) – temporal metrics are compared by GET /api/v1/compare, snapshot metrics by GET /api/v1/compare/snapshot.

  • metrics[].improves_on_chaoss (object, required)

  • metrics[].improves_on_chaoss.chaoss_url (string:uri, required)

  • metrics[].improves_on_chaoss.delta_note (string, required)

  • metrics[].our_reference_url (string:uri, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The catalog.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • Cache-Control (string) – public, max-age=3600.

GET /api/v1/compare
Operation:

comparison

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns one temporal metric’s series for up to seven repositories or organizations.

Each entity’s series is densified (every bucket present) from the later of since and the entity’s first activity (data_start) to until, so series of one answer may differ in length: align them by bucket. An organization is the union of its collected repositories (at most 500).

Every entity must be readable by the caller. A signed-in session that names a collected entity outside its groups has the entity’s collected repositories added to its “Comparisons” group, and the answer lists that in added_to_group (such an answer is not cached). An API token is refused instead (403 entity_out_of_scope, with the way to add the entity). Every compared repository a signed-in caller may read is also recorded in its “Comparisons” group, silently.

Whole answers are cached for 60 seconds per caller and query (X-Cache: hit). No ETag is sent.

Cost: one aggregate per entity and metric over the window, each entity’s series reused while its repositories’ collection state is unchanged.

Handler: handleCompare.

Query Parameters:

  • metric (string:enum, required) – A temporal id from the metric catalog.

  • entities (string, required) – Comma-separated, at most 7: repo:<id> or org:<host>/<login>.

  • since (string:date) – First day (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: the bucket boundary three years before until’s bucket. Unlike the repository routes, a value that does not parse is a 400.

  • until (string:date) – A day (YYYY-MM-DD; default today, UTC), never later than the latest plausible commit time, then truncated to the start of its week or month. The window ends there, exclusive, so the series ends at the last complete bucket before that day. A value that does not parse is a 400.

  • bucket (string:enum)

  • retention_threshold (integer) – contributor_retention only. Contributions (over all collected history) that make a contributor “repeat” rather than “drive-by”.

Response JSON Object:

  • metric (object, required) – One metric of the comparison catalog (MetricDef).

  • metric.id (string, required) – The value to pass as metric.

  • metric.name (string, required)

  • metric.definition (string, required)

  • metric.unit (string, required)

  • metric.kind (string:enum, required) – temporal metrics are compared by GET /api/v1/compare, snapshot metrics by GET /api/v1/compare/snapshot.

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss (object, required)

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss.chaoss_url (string:uri, required)

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss.delta_note (string, required)

  • metric.our_reference_url (string:uri, required)

  • bucket (string:enum, required)

  • since (string:date, required) – The effective window start.

  • until (string:date, required) – The effective window end (exclusive bucket boundary).

  • series[] (object) – One entity’s series (compareSeries).

  • series[].entity (object, required) – A compared repository or organization, as parsed from entities (entity).

  • series[].entity.kind (string:enum, required)

  • series[].entity.repo_id (integer:int64) – repo entities only.

  • series[].entity.host (string) – org entities only.

  • series[].entity.login (string) – org entities only.

  • series[].entity.label (string, required) – owner/name for a repository, login (org) for an organization; the raw entity token when the lookup of labels failed.

  • series[].points[] (object) – One bucket of a series (db.WeeklyPoint).

  • series[].points[].bucket (string:date-time, required) – The bucket’s first instant (UTC); a Monday for week, the 1st for month.

  • series[].points[].value (number, required)

  • series[].parts (object) – contributor_retention only: the component series drive_by and repeat, whose sum is points.

  • series[].parts.{part}[] (object) – One bucket of a series (db.WeeklyPoint).

  • series[].parts.{part}[].bucket (string:date-time, required) – The bucket’s first instant (UTC); a Monday for week, the 1st for month.

  • series[].parts.{part}[].value (number, required)

  • series[].data_start (string:date) – The entity’s first dateable activity (first issue, change request, commit, or the forge’s creation date). Absent when it has none.

  • added_to_group[] (object) – A one-time notice that this request added an entity’s collected repositories to one of the caller’s groups.

  • added_to_group[].entity (string, required) – The entity’s label.

  • added_to_group[].group (string, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The series.

  • 400 Bad Request – metric is not a temporal catalog id; entities is missing, malformed or longer than 7; a date does not parse; since is not before until; bucket is not week or month; or retention_threshold is not a positive integer.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – A compared entity resolves to no repository the caller may read (entity_out_of_scope; for an API token, with the way to add it), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response EntityOutOfScope.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Cache (string) – hit when the answer came from the server’s response cache; absent otherwise.

GET /api/v1/compare/snapshot
Operation:

comparisonSnapshot

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns one snapshot metric’s current value for up to seven repositories or organizations.

The same entities and scope rules as GET /api/v1/compare (automatic addition for a session, refusal for an API token, added_to_group). Not cached.

Handler: handleCompareSnapshot.

Query Parameters:

  • metric (string:enum, required) – A snapshot id from the metric catalog.

  • entities (string, required) – Comma-separated, at most 7: repo:<id> or org:<host>/<login>.

Response JSON Object:

  • metric (object, required) – One metric of the comparison catalog (MetricDef).

  • metric.id (string, required) – The value to pass as metric.

  • metric.name (string, required)

  • metric.definition (string, required)

  • metric.unit (string, required)

  • metric.kind (string:enum, required) – temporal metrics are compared by GET /api/v1/compare, snapshot metrics by GET /api/v1/compare/snapshot.

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss (object, required)

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss.chaoss_url (string:uri, required)

  • metric.improves_on_chaoss.delta_note (string, required)

  • metric.our_reference_url (string:uri, required)

  • values[] (object) – One entity’s snapshot value (db.SnapshotValue with its entity).

  • values[].entity (object, required) – A compared repository or organization, as parsed from entities (entity).

  • values[].entity.kind (string:enum, required)

  • values[].entity.repo_id (integer:int64) – repo entities only.

  • values[].entity.host (string) – org entities only.

  • values[].entity.login (string) – org entities only.

  • values[].entity.label (string, required) – owner/name for a repository, login (org) for an organization; the raw entity token when the lookup of labels failed.

  • added_to_group[] (object) – A one-time notice that this request added an entity’s collected repositories to one of the caller’s groups.

  • added_to_group[].entity (string, required) – The entity’s label.

  • added_to_group[].group (string, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – One value per entity, in request order.

  • 400 Bad Request – metric is not a snapshot catalog id, or entities is missing, malformed or longer than 7.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – A compared entity resolves to no repository the caller may read (entity_out_of_scope; for an API token, with the way to add it), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response EntityOutOfScope.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

entitySearchResults

Access:

Returns the repositories and organizations whose names match a query, for the comparison picker.

Up to 20 repositories (each classed in_scope, chartable now, or collected, which a session’s compare would add) and up to 10 organizations. Account

The signed-in caller’s identity, account e-mail and session.

GET /api/v1/me
Operation:

me

Access:

a signed-in session or an API token.

Returns the caller’s identity, account e-mail, role, scope size and fair-use numbers.

The identity fields and the account fields are best-effort: a failed lookup yields empty strings (logged), never an error. capacity is null when the store cannot answer. For an API token, capacity reports the token’s own allowances.

Handler: handleMe.

Response JSON Object:

  • user_id (integer, required)

  • login (string, required)

  • name (string, required)

  • avatar_url (string, required)

  • provider (string, required) – The forge of the account’s last sign-in (github, gitlab); empty when unknown.

  • email (string, required) – The confirmed account e-mail; empty when none.

  • email_pending (string, required) – An address waiting for its confirmation link; empty when none.

  • is_admin (boolean, required) – Always false for an API token.

  • capacity (object) – The caller’s fair-use numbers (meCapacity); request counts are this api process’s.

  • capacity.repos (object, required) – An account’s repository allocation (db.RepoAllocationStatus).

  • capacity.repos.used (integer, required) – Repositories across the account’s groups, additions waiting for approval included.

  • capacity.repos.allowed (integer, required)

GET /api/v1/me/sessions
Operation:

mySessions

Access:

a signed-in session; an API token is refused.

Returns the caller’s live sessions.

Every live session of the account (0.29.113, OWASP ASVS V7.5.2): the browser sessions of the web GUI (kind web), the tokens POST /api/v1/auth/token minted and the tokens the web process’s /api/ proxy holds (kind api; both are minted from a browser session: from_web_session is true while that session lives and false once it has expired, which the SPA’s 30-day token outlives). The session presenting this request is current. Operator-issued API tokens are not sessions and are not listed. A browser session idle past web.session_idle_minutes is not live and not listed. last_used_at moves, at most once a minute (every half bound when the bound is under two minutes), for kind web only; a token’s is its mint time.

Handler: handleMeSessions.

Response JSON Object:

  • sessions[] (object) – One live session of an account (0.29.113).

  • sessions[].kind (string:enum, required) – web is a browser session of the web GUI; api is a Bearer token.

  • sessions[].from_web_session (boolean, required) – The token’s browser session is still live (every kind api session is minted from one; false once it has expired, and for kind web).

  • sessions[].current (boolean, required) – This session presented the request.

  • sessions[].created_at (string:date-time, required) – When the session was signed in or the token minted.

  • sessions[].last_used_at (string:date-time, required) – A browser session’s last request, to the minute (created_at until its first); for kind api, the mint time.

  • sessions[].expires_at (string:date-time, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The sessions, newest first.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • Cache-Control (string)

a signed-in session; an API token is refused.

Ends every session of the caller’s account, this one included.

Deletes the account’s web sessions, /auth/token tokens and proxy tokens (0.29.113, OWASP ASVS V7.5.2): every other browser and client of the account is signed out at its next request, and this token’s next request is 401 too — the answer is the last one it gets. No body. Never refused by a spent request quota, and not counted (0.29.114), like sign-out.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

Operation:

Access:

a signed-in session; an API token is refused.

Stores an address as the account’s pending e-mail and mails its confirmation link.

The same submission the web process’s account page uses. A refusal the user can act on (not a deliverable address, mail not configured on this server, a failed save or send) is a 422 carrying the message the web form shows. Bodies over 4 KiB are refused.

  • email (string:email, required)

Response JSON Object:

  • sent (boolean, required)

Status Codes:

  • 403 Forbidden – An operator-issued API token (error is a sentence saying an API token cannot change account settings), or a sign-in older than web.session_idle_minutes (since 0.29.113, OWASP ASVS V7.5.1: error is reauthentication_required and message says what to do — the recovery address changes only after a recent sign-in; every session token is judged by the sign-in of the browser session it was minted from, and a token whose browser session expired has none that counts).

  • 422 Unprocessable Entity – Nothing was mailed; message says why, in the words the web form uses.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – A presented token could not be checked (session lookup failed; try again), or this server runs without a store (accounts unavailable), or the request ran past http_timeout_seconds (plain text).

a signed-in session; an API token is refused.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – The database failed; nothing changed and the link still works.

POST /api/v1/groups/{groupID}/repos
Operation:

addRepositoriesToGroup

Access:

a signed-in session or an API token.

Adds repositories, or one organization, to one of the caller’s groups.

kind repo (the default) adds urls (or the single url, used only when urls holds no non-empty entry): at most 1,000 per request, all in one step. Repositories already tracked are linked at once (linked); an administrator’s new repositories are queued for collection (enqueued); a non-administrator’s new ones wait for approval as one add request (pending_approval, request_id), unless they fit under web.auto_approve_add_limit.

kind org registers one organization (one URL per request). An administrator’s registration, or one of an organization already tracked elsewhere, answers registered: 1; otherwise the registration waits for approval (pending_approval: 1, request_id). The organization’s repositories are linked later, by the scheduler’s organization scan. A GitHub organization must be on this deployment’s GitHub host, and a GitLab group on its configured GitLab instance (gitlab.base_url).

Every line is parsed as a repository URL first (a missing scheme is supplied; GitHub, GitLab and any git host are accepted): a line that is not one is reported in invalid and skipped, the rest go through; a paste with no usable line is a 400.

An add that does not fit the account’s repository allocation (403) or its daily additions (429, quota repo_links_per_day, until 00:00 UTC) adds nothing and is refused with the capacity_limit body. A group that is not the caller’s is a 404; one an administrator rejected is a 409. A 500 naming how many repositories could not be added means some URLs failed while the others were added: send them again. The body is bounded (1,000 URLs at the store’s URL length).

Handler: handleGroupAddRepo.

Parameters:

  • groupID (integer:int64, required) – A group’s id.

Request JSON Object:

  • url (string) – One URL; ignored when urls holds a non-empty entry.

  • urls[] (string)

  • kind (string:enum) – Any value other than org adds repositories.

Response JSON Object:

  • ok (boolean, required)

  • submitted (integer, required) – The non-blank URLs received.

  • linked (integer) – Repositories only. Already-tracked repositories linked into the group.

  • enqueued (integer) – Repositories only. New repositories queued for collection.

  • pending_approval (integer) – Items waiting for an administrator (an organization counts 1).

  • request_id (integer:int64) – The add request holding the waiting items.

  • invalid[] (string)

  • registered (integer) – Organizations only. Tracking is registered now.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – What happened. For repositories: linked, enqueued, and when approval is needed pending_approval and request_id. For an organization: registered: 1, or pending_approval: 1 with request_id.

  • 400 Bad Request – The body is malformed or names no URL; no line of the paste is a repository URL; more than 1,000 URLs; more than one organization; a group id that is not an integer; an organization not on this deployment’s GitHub host or GitLab instance; a URL that is too long, carries credentials or was refused by the database.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The add would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Nothing was written.

  • 404 Not Found – No group of the caller’s has that id (no group of yours with that id).

  • 409 Conflict – An administrator rejected the group; it takes no additions.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – JSON error add request <id>: <f> of <n> repositories could not be added; try adding them again (f of the n URLs failed, the rest were added), or the generic server failure as plain text (internal error; try again; the cause is in the api log).

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

POST /api/v1/collections/{collectionID}/copy
Operation:

Access:

a signed-in session or an API token.

Links every repository of a collection into one of the caller’s groups.

Names the target by group_id or, when that is absent or 0, by group_name (found or created). The copy fits the caller’s repository allocation (else 403) and its daily additions (else 429, quota repo_links_per_day), or adds nothing. An id with no collection adds nothing (added 0).

Handler: handleCollectionCopy.

  • collectionID (integer:int64, required) – A collection’s id.

Request JSON Object:

  • group_id (integer:int64) – One of the caller’s groups.

Response JSON Object:

  • added (integer:int64, required)

  • group_id (integer:int64, required)

Status Codes:

  • 400 Bad Request – The id is not an integer, the body is not JSON, or neither group_id nor group_name is given.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The target group is not the caller’s (text/plain), or the copy does not fit the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation).

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

Operation:

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Ends every session of an account.

An administrator’s answer to a lost device or a suspected account takeover (0.29.113, OWASP ASVS V7.4.5): the account’s web sessions, /auth/token tokens and proxy tokens are deleted, and each is 401 at its next request. an administrator’s signed-in session.

An administrator cannot demote itself, and the last administrator is never demoted. The change applies to the account’s next request in this process.

POST /api/v1/admin/add-requests/{requestID}/{decision}
Operation:

decideAddRequest

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Approves or rejects an add request.

An approved repository request is processed in the background (repositories created, queued and linked); approving it again resumes an interrupted pass. An approved organization request registers tracking; the scheduler’s next organization scan links its repositories. A request already decided keeps its decision: deciding it again, in either direction, answers changed: false and changes nothing, except that approving an approved request again resumes an interrupted repository pass, or registers an organization whose registration an older release lost (then changed: true). The requester is mailed when the decision changed.

Handler: handleAdminAddRequestDecision.

Parameters:

  • requestID (integer:int64, required)

  • decision (string:enum, required)

Response JSON Object:

  • ok (boolean, required)

  • changed (boolean, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – Done.

  • 400 Bad Request – The request id is not an integer, or the decision is neither approve nor reject.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 404 Not Found – No such add request.

  • 409 Conflict – The group was rejected, or an organization cannot be registered (not on this deployment’s GitHub host or GitLab instance, a URL carrying credentials, or too long); the body says what to do.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

POST /api/v1/admin/api-tokens
Operation:

grantAPIToken

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Grants an API token to an account.

The answer is the only time the token is shown; it is sent Cache-Control: private, no-store. A token’s allowances are fixed when it is granted. Body limit 64 KiB.

Handler: handleAdminAPITokenGrant.

Request JSON Object:

  • user_id (integer, required) – The account the token authenticates as. A value above 2,147,483,647 is not refused as a 400; it currently fails as a 500.

  • label (string, required) – Who or what the token is for. Not blank; at most 200 characters after trimming.

  • lifetime_days (integer) – Default default_lifetime_days.

  • rate_limit_per_hour (integer) – Default default_rate_limit_per_hour.

  • rate_limit_per_day (integer) – Default default_rate_limit_per_day.

Response JSON Object:

  • token (string, required) – The API token (avx_…). Shown once.

  • token_id (integer:int64, required)

  • user_id (integer, required)

  • label (string, required)

  • created_at (string:date-time, required)

  • expires_at (string:date-time, required)

  • rate_limit_per_hour (integer, required)

  • rate_limit_per_day (integer, required)

Status Codes:

  • 201 Created – Granted.

  • 400 Bad Request – The body is not JSON; user_id is missing, not positive, above 2147483647 (0.29.100; it was a 500), or names no account; label is blank or too long; or a lifetime or allowance is out of range.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • Cache-Control (string) – private, no-store.

POST /api/v1/admin/api-tokens/{tokenID}/revoke
Operation:

revokeAPIToken

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Revokes an API token.

The token stops working on its next call to any api process (every API-token call rechecks it). Revoking a revoked token is a no-op.

Handler: handleAdminAPITokenRevoke.

Parameters:

  • tokenID (integer:int64, required)

Response JSON Object:

  • token_id (integer:int64, required)

  • revoked (boolean, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – Revoked.

  • 400 Bad Request – The id is not a positive integer.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 404 Not Found – No API token with that id.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

apiTokenSettings

an administrator’s signed-in session.

POST /api/v1/admin/api-token-settings
Operation:

updateAPITokenSettings

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Changes the defaults an API-token grant offers.

The allowances are the token_requests_per_hour and token_requests_per_day quotas. Changing the value of one that aveloxis.json sets is refused with 409; sending its current value (or omitting the daily one) is accepted. An omitted daily value is left unchanged. Tokens already granted keep their allowances. Body limit 64 KiB.

Handler: handleAdminAPITokenSettingsUpdate.

  • default_rate_limit_per_day (integer)

  • default_rate_limit_per_day (integer, required)

  • default_lifetime_days (integer, required)

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

GET /api/v1/admin/forge-id-changes
Operation:

forgeIDChanges

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Returns the recorded forge-ID changes.

A repository deleted and re-created upstream under the same URL gets a new forge ID; the organization scan records it as pending. The full list orders adoptable, superseded, then adopted changes. A pending change whose old ID is no longer the stored one is superseded and cannot be adopted.

Handler: handleAdminForgeIDChanges.

Query Parameters:

  • pending (string) – 1 lists only the adoptable changes; any other value lists all.

Response JSON Object:

  • changes[] (object) – A recorded forge-ID change (db.ForgeIDChange).

  • changes[].repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • changes[].old_forge_id (string, required)

  • changes[].new_forge_id (string, required)

  • changes[].first_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • changes[].last_observed_at (string:date-time, required)

  • changes[].forge_created_at (string:date-time) – When the forge created the new repository; absent when the scan did not list it.

  • changes[].adopted_at (string:date-time) – Adopted changes only.

  • changes[].adopted_by (string)

  • changes[].note (string)

  • changes[].repo_git (string) – The repository’s stored URL.

  • changes[].superseded (boolean) – A pending change whose old ID is no longer the stored one; it cannot be adopted. Absent when false.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The changes.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – forge-ID changes could not be listed.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

POST /api/v1/admin/forge-id-changes/{repoID}/adopt
Operation:

adoptForgeIDChange

Access:

an administrator’s signed-in session.

Adopts a recorded forge-ID change, treating the new upstream repository as a continuation.

Moves the stored forge ID to the one the scan observed and records the administrator. The body names the change, since a repository can have more than one. The api process holds no forge keys, so this adopts the recorded observation; aveloxis adopt-forge-id asks the forge live. The body is at most 6,256 bytes and the note at most 1,000 bytes.

Handler: handleAdminForgeIDAdopt.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Request JSON Object:

  • old_forge_id (string, required)

  • new_forge_id (string, required)

  • note (string) – At most 1,000 bytes.

Response JSON Object:

  • adopted (boolean, required)

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – Adopted.

  • 400 Bad Request – The repository id is not a positive integer, the body is unreadable, too large or not JSON, an ID is missing, or the note is too long.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Shared response Forbidden.

  • 404 Not Found – No unadopted change with that pair is recorded for this repository.

  • 409 Conflict – Superseded; the repository no longer stores the old ID. Nothing was written.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.
