GET /api/v1/repo-groups
Operation:

augurRepositoryGroups

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns every repository group, ordered by name.

The legacy repository groups (aveloxis_data.repo_groups), not the caller’s own groups (see Groups). An API token sees only the groups holding at least one repository of its owner’s groups (since 0.29.99); every other caller sees every group. An empty result is [].

Handler: handleRepoGroups.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • repo_group_id (integer:int64, required)

  • rg_name (string, required)

  • description (string) – Absent when empty.

  • rg_type (string) – Absent when empty (for example github_org, gitlab_group).

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The repository groups.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

GET /api/v1/repos
Operation:

augurRepositories

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns every collected repository, ordered by owner and name.

Not paged: one row per repository. An API token sees only the repositories of its owner’s groups (since 0.29.99); a session, an administrator and a caller without an identity get the whole catalog. Cost: one scan of the repositories table. An empty result is [].

Handler: handleAllRepos.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • repo_id (integer:int64, required)

  • repo_group_id (integer:int64, required) – 0 when the repository has no legacy group.

  • repo_git (string, required) – The repository’s URL.

  • repo_name (string, required)

  • repo_owner (string, required)

  • platform_id (integer:enum, required) – 1 GitHub, 2 GitLab, 3 any other git host.

  • repo_archived (boolean, required)

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The repositories.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}
Operation:

augurRepository

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns one repository’s identity fields.

The body is the internal repository record without JSON tags, so its keys are PascalCase, unlike the other catalog lookups. Only ID, Platform, GitURL, Name and Owner are read from the database; every other field carries its zero value (GroupID 0, empty strings, false, 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z).

Handler: handleRepoByID.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Response JSON Object:

  • ID (integer:int64, required)

  • GroupID (integer:int64, required) – Always 0 here.

  • Platform (integer:enum, required) – 1 GitHub, 2 GitLab, 3 any other git host.

  • GitURL (string, required)

  • Name (string, required)

  • Owner (string, required)

  • Path (string, required) – Always empty here.

  • Description (string, required) – Always empty here.

  • PrimaryLanguage (string, required) – Always empty here.

  • ForkedFrom (string, required) – Always empty here.

  • Archived (boolean, required) – Always false here.

  • CreatedAt (string:date-time, required) – Always 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z here.

  • UpdatedAt (string:date-time, required) – Always 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z here.

  • PlatformID (string, required) – Always empty here.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The repository.

  • 400 Bad Request – repoID is not a positive integer (invalid repo_id).

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found).

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

Augur metrics

Augur-compatible per-repository metrics, with Augur’s parameter names (begin_date, end_date, period).

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/issues-new
Operation:

augurIssuesNew

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the issues opened per period.

Issues (pull requests excluded) counted by the day they were created. The window is begin_date through end_date, both inclusive UTC days (since 0.29.99; before, end_date ended at that day’s midnight), by default the year before today through today. A date that does not parse as YYYY-MM-DD is a 400. period buckets by day, week, month or year; it defaults to month, and any other value is read as month (no 400). An empty result is [].

Handler: handleIssuesNew.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • begin_date (string:date) – Augur’s window start, an inclusive UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD). Default a year before today; a value that does not parse is a 400 (since 0.29.99).

  • end_date (string:date) – Augur’s window end, an inclusive UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD; the whole day counts, since 0.29.99). Default today; a value that does not parse is a 400.

  • period (string) – Augur’s bucket size, day, week, month or year. Any other value is read as month, never refused.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • date (string:date-time, required) – The bucket’s first day (midnight UTC), or the snapshot’s collection time.

  • value (integer, required)

  • repo_name (string) – Absent when empty.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – One row per bucket that has activity, oldest first.

  • 400 Bad Request – repoID is not a positive integer (invalid repo_id).

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/deps
Operation:

augurDependencies

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the repository’s dependencies with their libyear.

With neither license nor scope, every stored dependency row, ordered by name. With either, the rows the licenses table aggregates (GitHub Actions rows excluded), so a license bucket counting N lists exactly N rows. An empty result is [].

Handler: handleDeps.

Request Headers:

  • If-None-Match (string) – An ETag from an earlier answer. When it names the current one the answer is 304 with no body.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • license (string) – Keep only rows whose license normalizes to this canonical bucket, exactly as /repos/{repoID}/licenses returned it.

  • scope (string:enum) – runtime keeps only runtime-scope dependencies (dev, test, build, optional and peer rows excluded); all keeps every scope. Any other value is a 400.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • name (string, required)

  • requirement (string, required) – The declared requirement; empty when none was recorded.

  • dep_type (string, required) – The dependency’s scope as recorded (for example runtime, dev); empty when unknown.

  • package_manager (string, required)

  • current_version (string, required)

  • latest_version (string, required)

  • libyear (number, required) – Years between the used version’s release and the latest’s; 0 when unknown.

  • license (string) – The license as the registry reported it (not normalized). Absent when unknown.

  • purl (string) – The package URL. Absent when none was minted.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The dependency rows.

  • 304 Not Modified – The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. Shared response NotModified.

  • 400 Bad Request – repoID is not a positive integer, or scope is neither all nor runtime.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • ETag (string) – The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

  • Cache-Control (string:enum) – no-cache for an answer any caller may be given (revalidate each time); private, no-store for an answer about this caller, which nothing may store.

  • X-Cache (string) – hit when the answer came from the server’s response cache; absent otherwise.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • name (string, required)

  • requirement (string, required) – The declared requirement; empty when none was recorded.

  • dep_type (string, required) – The dependency’s scope as recorded (for example runtime, dev); empty when unknown.

  • package_manager (string, required)

  • current_version (string, required)

  • latest_version (string, required)

  • libyear (number, required) – Years between the used version’s release and the latest’s; 0 when unknown.

  • license (string) – The license as the registry reported it (not normalized). Absent when unknown.

  • purl (string) – The package URL. Absent when none was minted.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – The dependency rows.

  • 304 Not Modified – The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. Shared response NotModified.

  • 400 Bad Request – repoID is not a positive integer, or scope is neither all nor runtime.

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • ETag (string) – The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

  • Cache-Control (string:enum) – no-cache for an answer any caller may be given (revalidate each time); private, no-store for an answer about this caller, which nothing may store.

  • X-Cache (string) – hit when the answer came from the server’s response cache; absent otherwise.

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/repo-messages
Operation:

augurRepositoryMessages

Access:

a session or an API token; anonymous callers too while api.require_auth is off or from an exempt network.

Returns the messages posted per period.

Every stored message of the repository (issue, pull request and review comments) counted by its timestamp. The window is begin_date through end_date, both inclusive UTC days (since 0.29.99; before, end_date ended at that day’s midnight), by default the year before today through today. A date that does not parse as YYYY-MM-DD is a 400. period buckets by day, week, month or year; it defaults to month, and any other value is read as month (no 400). An empty result is [].

Handler: handleRepoMessages.

Parameters:

  • repoID (integer:int64, required) – A repository’s id (repo_id). A value that is not a positive integer is a 400; an id no repository has is a 404 on every repository route (since 0.29.99).

Query Parameters:

  • begin_date (string:date) – Augur’s window start, an inclusive UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD). Default a year before today; a value that does not parse is a 400 (since 0.29.99).

  • end_date (string:date) – Augur’s window end, an inclusive UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD; the whole day counts, since 0.29.99). Default today; a value that does not parse is a 400.

  • period (string) – Augur’s bucket size, day, week, month or year. Any other value is read as month, never refused.

Response JSON Array of Objects:

  • date (string:date-time, required) – The bucket’s first day (midnight UTC), or the snapshot’s collection time.

  • value (integer, required)

  • repo_name (string) – Absent when empty.

Status Codes:

  • 200 OK – One row per bucket that has activity, oldest first.

  • 400 Bad Request – repoID is not a positive integer (invalid repo_id).

  • 401 Unauthorized – No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Shared response Unauthorized.

  • 403 Forbidden – The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Shared response RepoOutOfScope.

  • 404 Not Found – No repository has this id (repo not found). Shared response RepoNotFound.

  • 429 Too Many Requests – Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. Shared response TooManyRequests.

  • 500 Internal Server Error – A server-side failure. Shared response ServerError.

  • 503 Service Unavailable – Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Shared response ServiceUnavailable.

Response Headers:

  • X-Aveloxis-Added-To-Group (string) – Present once, on the answer whose request added the repository to the caller’s “Shared with Me” group (a signed-in session following a link to a repository outside its groups). Its value is the group’s name. The addition happens before the operation runs, so the header rides on whatever that request answers, a 400, 404, 429 or 500 included; the reference declares it on the success response.

Shared responses

Responses many operations share, written once. An entry above that links here sends exactly this response; the conventions say what each status code means across the API.

NotModified

The If-None-Match validator names the current answer. No body.

Headers:

  • ETag (string) — The answer’s validator, weak (W/"…") when the answer depends only on the repository’s stored state. Send it back as If-None-Match.

BadRequest

The request is malformed (an id that is not an integer, a value outside its enum, a missing parameter). The body is one sentence.

Body, text/plain: string

Unauthorized

No valid Bearer token: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. Sent by every operation that requires an identity, and by every data operation when api.require_auth is on (callers on an exempt network excepted). Never stored.

Body, application/json (Error):

  • error (string, required) — A machine-readable code or a sentence; see each operation.

  • message (string) — A sentence for a person, present when error is a code (reauthentication_required).

Forbidden

The token is valid but may not do this: an API token on an administrator or account-settings route, or a session that is not an administrator’s. Never stored.

Body, application/json (Error):

  • error (string, required) — A machine-readable code or a sentence; see each operation.

  • message (string) — A sentence for a person, present when error is a code (reauthentication_required).

RepoOutOfScope

The repository is outside the caller’s scope (repo_out_of_scope), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition of it would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Never stored.

Body, application/json:

One of:

  • RepoOutOfScope

    • error (string, required) — always repo_out_of_scope

    • repo_id (integer, int64, required)

    • hint (string, required)

    • repo_url (string) — API tokens only, when the repository exists. Its stored URL.

    • your_groups (array of object) — The owner’s groups that accept additions.

      • group_id (integer, int64, required)

      • name (string, required)

    • add_to_existing_group (object) — A request ready to send.

      • method (string, required) — always POST

      • path (string, required) — The path, with {group_id} to fill in where present.

      • body (object, required) — The JSON body: {"url": …, "kind": "repo"} for one repository, {"urls": […], "kind": "repo"} for an organization’s collected repositories, {"name": …} for a new group.

    • create_group (object) — A request ready to send.

      • method (string, required) — always POST

      • path (string, required) — The path, with {group_id} to fill in where present.

      • body (object, required) — The JSON body: {"url": …, "kind": "repo"} for one repository, {"urls": […], "kind": "repo"} for an organization’s collected repositories, {"name": …} for a new group.

  • CapacityRefusal

    • error (string, required) — always capacity_limit

    • kind (string, required) — one of rate, allocation

    • quota (string, required) — one of requests_per_hour, requests_per_day, token_requests_per_hour, token_requests_per_day, repos_per_account, repo_links_per_day, shared_with_me_adds_per_hour; The quota that refused.

    • window (string) — one of hour, day; Rate quotas only. hour starts at the window’s first counted request; day is the UTC day.

    • used (integer, required)

    • allowed (integer, required)

    • wanted (integer) — Allocation only. How many more the refused change would have added.

    • reset_at (string, date-time) — Rate quotas only. When the window ends (UTC).

    • retry_after (integer) — Rate quotas only. Seconds until reset_at, the same value as Retry-After.

    • contact (string) — The address the operator invites heavy users to write to; absent when none is set.

    • message (string, required) — The refusal in a sentence, with the way to make room or the time to retry.

EntityOutOfScope

A compared entity resolves to no repository the caller may read (entity_out_of_scope; for an API token, with the way to add it), or a signed-in session’s automatic addition would exceed the account’s repository allocation (capacity_limit, kind allocation). Never stored.

Body, application/json:

One of:

  • EntityOutOfScope

    • error (string, required) — always entity_out_of_scope

    • entity (string, required) — The entity’s label.

    • hint (string, required)

    • entity_url (string) — API tokens, repository entities only. The repository’s stored URL.

    • entity_repo_urls (array of string) — API tokens, organization entities only. The organization’s collected repositories, all added by add_to_existing_group in one call.

    • your_groups (array of object) — The owner’s groups that accept additions.

      • group_id (integer, int64, required)

      • name (string, required)

    • add_to_existing_group (object) — A request ready to send.

      • method (string, required) — always POST

      • path (string, required) — The path, with {group_id} to fill in where present.

      • body (object, required) — The JSON body: {"url": …, "kind": "repo"} for one repository, {"urls": […], "kind": "repo"} for an organization’s collected repositories, {"name": …} for a new group.

    • create_group (object) — A request ready to send.

      • method (string, required) — always POST

      • path (string, required) — The path, with {group_id} to fill in where present.

      • body (object, required) — The JSON body: {"url": …, "kind": "repo"} for one repository, {"urls": […], "kind": "repo"} for an organization’s collected repositories, {"name": …} for a new group.

  • CapacityRefusal

    • error (string, required) — always capacity_limit

    • kind (string, required) — one of rate, allocation

    • quota (string, required) — one of requests_per_hour, requests_per_day, token_requests_per_hour, token_requests_per_day, repos_per_account, repo_links_per_day, shared_with_me_adds_per_hour; The quota that refused.

    • window (string) — one of hour, day; Rate quotas only. hour starts at the window’s first counted request; day is the UTC day.

    • used (integer, required)

    • allowed (integer, required)

    • wanted (integer) — Allocation only. How many more the refused change would have added.

    • reset_at (string, date-time) — Rate quotas only. When the window ends (UTC).

    • retry_after (integer) — Rate quotas only. Seconds until reset_at, the same value as Retry-After.

    • contact (string) — The address the operator invites heavy users to write to; absent when none is set.

    • message (string, required) — The refusal in a sentence, with the way to make room or the time to retry.

NotFound

No such resource.

Body, text/plain: string

RepoNotFound

No repository has this id (repo not found). Every repository route answers it before deciding the caller’s scope (since 0.29.99; an unknown id was a 403 for tokens and sessions before), so it says nothing about the caller.

Body, text/plain: string

TooManyRequests

Refused by a rate limit; retry after Retry-After seconds. A caller without a valid token is limited per address (api.rate_limit_rps, api.rate_limit_burst, api.rate_limit_daily) and gets the plain text rate limit exceeded. A session or an API token is limited by its quotas and gets the capacity_limit body, sent Cache-Control: private, no-store; so does a session’s automatic addition past shared_with_me_adds_per_hour, and an operation that links repositories into a group past the account’s repo_links_per_day. The per-address text carries no cache directive.

Headers:

  • Retry-After (integer) — Whole seconds until the refused request may succeed (at least 1).

  • RateLimit (string) — The tightest enforced quota this answer was counted against (IETF RateLimit header fields draft): "<quota>";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds to reset>. Sent on every answer counted against an enforced quota of a session or an API token; a quota in shadow mode is not advertised.

  • RateLimit-Policy (string) — Every enforced quota the answer was counted against: "<quota>";q=<allowed>;w=<window seconds>, comma-separated.

  • X-RateLimit-Limit (integer) — The tightest enforced quota’s allowance (the older header, kept for clients that read it).

  • X-RateLimit-Remaining (integer) — Requests left in the tightest enforced quota’s window.

  • X-RateLimit-Reset (integer, int64) — When the tightest enforced quota’s window ends, in Unix seconds.

Body, application/json (CapacityRefusal):

  • error (string, required) — always capacity_limit

  • kind (string, required) — one of rate, allocation

  • quota (string, required) — one of requests_per_hour, requests_per_day, token_requests_per_hour, token_requests_per_day, repos_per_account, repo_links_per_day, shared_with_me_adds_per_hour; The quota that refused.

  • window (string) — one of hour, day; Rate quotas only. hour starts at the window’s first counted request; day is the UTC day.

  • used (integer, required)

  • allowed (integer, required)

  • wanted (integer) — Allocation only. How many more the refused change would have added.

  • reset_at (string, date-time) — Rate quotas only. When the window ends (UTC).

  • retry_after (integer) — Rate quotas only. Seconds until reset_at, the same value as Retry-After.

  • contact (string) — The address the operator invites heavy users to write to; absent when none is set.

  • message (string, required) — The refusal in a sentence, with the way to make room or the time to retry.

Body, text/plain: rate limit exceeded and a newline (the per-address limit).

ServerError

A server-side failure. The body never carries the cause (internal error; try again, or a fixed phrase); the cause is in the api log.

Body, text/plain: string

ServiceUnavailable

Retry later; this is never a sign-out. Either a presented token could not be checked because the database failed (JSON, session lookup failed; try again), or the request ran past http_timeout_seconds and was cut off (plain text, request exceeded http_timeout_seconds).

Body, application/json (Error):

  • error (string, required) — A machine-readable code or a sentence; see each operation.

  • message (string) — A sentence for a person, present when error is a code (reauthentication_required).

Body, text/plain: request exceeded http_timeout_seconds and a newline.
